B An ape's diet necessarily implies certain facts about their evolutionary history.
C The fact that apes ate fruit is good evidence for whether or not they stood upright.

initial.html:
Question 4

Noa: During the Early Miocene era, fruit grew on the peripheries of tree canopies. To reach them, apes would have had to distribute their weight equally on their two back legs, a task much more easily accomplished by a primate capable of standing upright. Thus, apes evolved to stand upright in order to eat fruit.

Kai: Your argument is unconvincing, as it places you at odds with recently uncovered evidence. Fossil records now show that Early Miocene apes ate a diet consisting exclusively of leaves and grasses.

Which one of the following is a point at issue between Noa and Kai?

initial.html:
Question 8

Noa: During the Early Miocene era, fruit grew on the peripheries of tree canopies. To reach them, apes would have had to distribute their weight equally on their two back legs, a task much more easily accomplished by a primate capable of standing upright. Thus, apes evolved to stand upright in order to eat fruit.

Kai: Your argument is unconvincing, as it places you at odds with recently uncovered evidence. Fossil records now show that Early Miocene apes ate a diet consisting exclusively of leaves and grasses.

On the basis of their statements, Noa and Kai are committed to agreeing about which one of the following?

To reach them, apes would have had to distribute their weight equally on their two back legs, a task much more easily accomplished by a primate capable of standing upright. Thus, apes evolved to stand upright in order to eat fruit.

Kai: Your argument is unconvincing, as it places you at odds with recently uncovered evidence. Fossil records now show that Early Miocene apes ate a diet consisting exclusively of leaves and grasses.

On the basis of their statements, Noa and Kai are committed to agreeing about which one of the following?

Correct! You got it right on the first try!
A

Early Miocene apes lived in areas with access to plant matter.

B

Early Miocene apes were able to distribute their weight equally across each limb.

C

Early Miocene apes lived near the peripheries of tree canopies.
